note: Add Another stores all state in the single config object addanother.settings. Global defaults for new content types are default_button/default_message/default_tab/default_tab_edit; per-content-type overrides are keyed by node type as button.<type>, message.<type>, tab.<type>, tab_edit.<type>. Two permissions: 'administer add another' (settings form addanother.admin_config -> /admin/config/content/addanother) and 'use add another' (see button/message/tab). Medium/hard cases are grounded in that real config object and use existing content types (article, blog_post). The site's addanother.settings may be empty; scripts write explicit values and cleanup restores the shipped install defaults (all default_* = true, empty per-type sequences).

evals.prompt: In the Drupal contrib module Add Another (addanother), where is the choice of whether a given content type shows the 'Save and add another' button stored? Name the config object and the key used for a per-content-type override.
evals.expected_output: It is stored in the config object addanother.settings. The per-content-type override lives at button.<type> (e.g. button.article), falling back to the global default_button when unset.

evals.prompt: Which permissions does the Add Another (addanother) Drupal module define, and what does each control?
evals.expected_output: 'administer add another' controls access to the settings form and configuring content types; 'use add another' controls whether a user actually sees and can use the 'Save and add another' button, the after-save message, and the 'Add another' tab.

evals.prompt: On a Drupal site with the Add Another module, where do I set the site-wide defaults (button, message, tab) that apply to new content types?
evals.expected_output: On the settings form at /admin/config/content/addanother (route addanother.admin_config), which edits default_button, default_message, default_tab and default_tab_edit in addanother.settings. Per-type overrides are edited on each content type's own edit form.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, the Article content type has an explicit Add Another override for the 'Save and add another' button that differs from the site default. Inspect the live addanother.settings configuration and state whether the button is enabled or disabled for Article.
evals.expected_output: It is disabled: addanother.settings has button.article = false, overriding the default_button (true).

evals.prompt: On this site, the Add Another after-save message has been configured specifically for the Blog post (blog_post) content type. Inspect the live addanother.settings config and state whether blog_post shows the 'Add another' message after a node is saved.
evals.expected_output: It does not show it: addanother.settings has message.blog_post = false.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, use the Add Another module to enable the 'Save and add another' button for the Article content type. Apply the change to the live site's addanother.settings configuration.
evals.expected_output: addanother.settings has button.article = true (set the key via drush cset addanother.settings button.article 1, config API, or by ticking 'Display Add another button on node add form' in the Article type's Add another settings).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, use the Add Another module to turn on the 'Add another' local-task tab for the Blog post (blog_post) content type, so nodes of that type get an 'Add another' tab. Apply the change to the live addanother.settings configuration.
evals.expected_output: addanother.settings has tab.blog_post = true (set via drush cset addanother.settings tab.blog_post 1, config API, or by ticking 'Display the Add another tab' in the blog_post type's Add another settings).
